title: Read replicas, replication lag and reading your own write

videos.script: Most of what a shop's database does is answer reads. {{reads}} A read replica is a second server that answers them too. It holds a copy of every row, and keeps it current by replaying every change the primary writes. {{copy}} In this lesson you build one on your own machine, in two commands, and point a query at it. {{build}} Then you meet the catch. The copy is always of a moment that has passed. Usually a few milliseconds ago. Sometimes much longer. {{lag}} You measure that lag from both ends, and find the reading that lies when nobody is writing. {{measure}} Then you make the lag ten seconds long, on purpose, and watch what a customer would see. They cancel an order. The page reloads. The order is still pending. {{stale}} There are two honest fixes, and you run one of them: wait until the replica has replayed the write, and only then read. {{fix}} Last, the replica pushes back. A long report on it collides with the cleaning the primary does, and the replica cancels the report. Stop that, and the primary pays instead. {{conflict}}
